doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago repertoire, bands and the end of the big-band era
title: Recording ban's non-effect on Chicago players
summary: Most Chicago musicians were not recording and only touring bigname bands got records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: This recording ban, it didn’t have an effect on you personally, because you weren’t recording then, right?
No, right. Most of the cats around Chicago were not recording.
So it had no effect on them.
No. See, then, if you had a record, you were like in the big leagues, because record companies were only hiring touring bands that had big names and things like that.
Not like today, where everybody can make a record.
Oh no. They’re even burning their own CDs.
